analysis.one_liner: Siemens Ltd (NSE: SIEMENS) is the Indian listed arm of Siemens AG Germany, making industrial automation, electrification, smart infrastructure and rail mobility equipment for utilities, industry and railways.
analysis.whats_happening: In the quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹5,734 crore but profit grew only 3.9% to ₹504 crore, as management and analysts pointed to rising commodity and currency (INR) costs squeezing margins. New order inflow jumped 37.8% to ₹6,228 crore and the order backlog rose 12% to ₹47,034 crore. An analyst/investor call is scheduled for November 20, 2026, two days from today.
analysis.plain_terms: Siemens India is winning more orders and selling more, but each rupee of sales is turning into less profit than before because input costs and currency moves are eating into margins. At the same time, the stock trades at roughly 89 times earnings - well above its own five-year average of about 69-75x. That is the tension: the market is paying a premium price for a business whose near-term profitability is currently weaker, betting that the large order backlog eventually restores margins.
analysis.quarters: Latest quarter (Sep 2026): revenue +17% YoY to ₹5,734cr, PAT +3.9% to ₹504cr, operating margin down YoY on commodity/FX cost pressure. Prior quarter (Mar 2026, the final quarter of an 18-month transition period as the company shifted its fiscal year from Oct-Sept to Apr-Mar): revenue +14.6% to ₹4,618cr but PAT fell 9.6% to ₹355cr, with profit from operations down 15% on commodity/FX costs plus restructuring charges. Note: this fiscal year's profit also includes a one-off ₹2,099 crore gain booked from the June 2026 cash sale of the Low Voltage Motors business to Innomotics - this is not operating profit and should be stripped out when judging run-rate earnings. Segment-level splits for the two most recent quarters could not be verified; treat as Not verified - check on Screener.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 25.1% from its October 16, 2024 peak and has returned just 7.6% over the past year versus peer ABB's 35.7% and the Nifty's -2.8%; over 5 years it is up 162% versus ABB's 227%. Importantly, Siemens Energy India was demerged out of this company (effective March 25, 2025), after the October 2024 peak - shareholders received Siemens Energy India shares separately, and this stock's price series does not add that value back. So part of the post-peak drawdown reflects value transferred to a now-separately-listed entity rather than value destroyed. The precise amount to add back to get a true like-for-like return is Not verified - check Siemens Energy India's (listed as ENERGY/ENRIN) price on Screener and the demerger swap ratio. Even allowing for this, 1-year performance has lagged the peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At last close of ₹3,480, the stock trades near a P/E of ~89x, against a cited five-year average in the 69-75x range across different data sources (the range itself is inconsistent, so treat as approximate). Why it is expensive: the market appears to be pricing in the ₹47,034 crore order backlog and 37.8% order inflow growth, not the current margin-compressed, demerger-adjusted earnings base, which also carries a one-off gain that flatters reported PAT. Whether that premium is justified depends on margins actually recovering as the backlog converts to revenue - it is not justified by current profitability alone.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently volume-led, not margin-led: revenue (+17% YoY) and new orders (+37.8% YoY) are both rising, but operating margins have fallen in both of the last two reported quarters due to commodity and currency costs. This is a healthier growth mix than margin-only expansion, but the margin pressure means profit growth (+3.9%) is lagging revenue growth meaningfully, and that gap is the thing to watch.
analysis.health_read: Siemens India carries very little debt (debt-to-equity reported around 2%) and reported ROCE of roughly 19.5% and ROE of roughly 14.4%, consistent with a conservatively financed business. The precise net cash figure quoted across sources was inconsistent (unit discrepancies), so the exact cash pile is Not verified - check the balance sheet on Screener directly. The real risk here is operational/business risk - commodity and currency cost pass-through squeezing margins - rather than financial or balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding stands at roughly 75% (Siemens International Holding B.V., Siemens AG Germany, and Siemens Metals Technologies Vermögensverwaltungs GmbH together), with zero pledging reported - typical of an MNC subsidiary structure. FII holding is roughly 6.5-6.8% and DII holding roughly 8.6-9.1%, both reportedly rising slightly in the latest quarter, though the exact FII figure varied slightly across sources. No marquee individual or star fund-manager stake was found on the shareholding register - none should be assumed.
strengths: Order backlog of ₹47,034 crore, up 12% YoY, with new order inflow up 37.8% YoY last quarter
Revenue growth of 17% YoY in the latest reported quarter, driven by volumes rather than price/margin alone
Zero promoter pledging on a 75% promoter stake
watchpoints: Operating margin fell YoY in both of the last two reported quarters on commodity and currency cost pressure
Trading at ~89x P/E versus a five-year average cited around 69-75x, a meaningful premium to its own history
Reported profit this fiscal year includes a one-off ₹2,099 crore gain from the Innomotics LVM business sale (June 2026) that will not repeat and overstates run-rate earnings
Stock has underperformed peer ABB over both 1 year (+7.6% vs +35.7%) and 5 years (+162% vs +227%), even after allowing for the Siemens Energy demerger distortion
analysis.one_thing: Whether operating margin stabilizes or recovers over the next one to two quarters - this is the single data point (watch the November 20, 2026 analyst call and the next quarterly results) that will show whether the commodity/FX cost pressure is temporary or structural, and whether the current premium valuation is earned.
